steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Concept: Glaciated upland landscapes are attractive for tourism, recreation and economic development because of their dramatic scenery, distinctive landforms and sense of wilderness. However, their fragile environments and limited accessibility create challenges. | Key Fact: The Lake District receives approximately 18 million visitors per year, generating an estimated £1.4 billion for the local economy and supporting around 18,000 jobs. Tourism accounts for roughly 40% of the Lake District's economy. | Key Concept: The multiple uses of glaciated uplands create conflicts between different interest groups. Tourists, farmers, conservationists, quarrying companies, foresters and local residents all want different things from the same landscape. | Key Facts: The Lake District National Park

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe two economic activities in glaciated upland areas. (4 marks) | Explain why land use conflicts arise in glaciated uplands. (4 marks) | Using a named glaciated upland area, describe the management strategies used to reduce conflict. (6 marks)

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Key Concept, Key Concept, Key Facts, and one past-paper question.
